audited_existing_suppliers.current_item_clause_excerpt_verbatim:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. On a probability space
$(\Omega,\mathcal F,P)$, a **continuous-time filtration** is a family
$(\mathcal F_t)_{t\ge0}$ of sub-sigma-algebras of $\mathcal F$ such that
$\mathcal F_s\subseteq\mathcal F_t$ whenever $0\le s\le t$. A process
$X=(X_t)_{t\ge0}$ is **adapted** when $X_t$ is measurable from
$(\Omega,\mathcal F_t)$ to its state space at every $t$.

For any process of random elements $X=(X_t)_{t\ge0}$, its **natural
filtration** is

$$\mathcal F_t^X=\sigma\!\left(\{X_u^{-1}(C):0\le u\le t,\ C\text{ measurable in the state space of }X_u\}\right).$$

The generated sigma-algebra exists by
[[thm-generated-sigma-algebra-exists-and-is-minimal]]. Its generator families
are nested in $t$, so $(\mathcal F_t^X)_{t\ge0}$ is a filtration; every
$X_t$ is $\mathcal F_t^X$-measurable, and minimality makes this the smallest
filtration to which $X$ is adapted. No completion or right-continuous
augmentation is included.

A real process $M=(M_t)_{t\ge0}$ is an **all-pairs continuous-time
martingale** relative to $(\mathcal F_t)$ when:

1. $M$ is adapted;
2. $E|M_t|<\infty$ for every $t\ge0$; and
3. for every $0\le s\le t$,
   $$E[M_t\mid\mathcal F_s]=M_s\qquad\text{almost surely}.$$

The equality in clause 3 is equality of the almost-everywhere classes in
[[def-conditional-expectation-as-an-ae-class]]. At $s=t$ it is the
known-variable identity. The word “continuous-time” specifies the index set;
it does not assert path continuity. Likewise the definition imposes neither
right continuity nor completeness on the filtration. AC is declared exactly
because the library's conditional-expectation existence theorem uses it; the
filtration, adaptation, and natural-filtration constructions make no choices.

pairs.proposal_text_verbatim: **Pages:** independent-subject-terminal-influence-limits / independent-subject-terminal-influence-limits-examples. **A, new earlier Cat-2 supplier:** Let $O_i$ be iid subjects and $\phi(O_i)\in\mathbb R^d$ satisfy $E\phi=0$, finite covariance $\Sigma$, and a separately proved expansion $\sqrt n(\hat\theta-\theta)=n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n\phi(O_i)+o_P(1)$. Then the published multivariate iid CLT and Slutsky give $N_d(0,\Sigma)$. For $G$ independent iid groups with $n_g/n\to\rho_g\in(0,1)$, if the expansion is $\sum_g\sqrt{n/n_g}\,n_g^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^{n_g}\phi_g(O_{gi})+o_P(1)$, each $E\phi_g=0$, and covariances are finite, the limit covariance is $\sum_g\rho_g^{-1}\operatorname{Var}(\phi_g)$. This theorem never supplies an influence expansion: each consumer must prove its own risk-set/random-denominator remainder. findings_and_repairs: Pair contract reviewed; exact claims, prerequisites, source ranges and proof obligations are transcribed below.
pairs.proposal_text_verbatim: **Pages:** nelson-aalen-kaplan-meier-greenwood / nelson-aalen-kaplan-meier-greenwood-examples. **A:** For right-censored iid subjects let $N_i(t)=1\{U_i\le t,\delta_i=1\}$, $Y_i(t)=1\{U_i\ge t\}$, $N=\sum_iN_i$, $Y=\sum_iY_i$, $dN(t)=\sum_i dN_i(t)$, and fix left/right endpoint conventions. Define $\hat\Lambda(t)=\int_{[0,t]}1\{Y(u)>0\}Y(u)^{-1}dN(u)$, $\hat S(t)=\prod_{u\le t:Y(u)>0}(1-dN(u)/Y(u))$, and Greenwood estimate $\hat S(t)^2\sum_{u\le t}dN(u)/\{Y(u)(Y(u)-dN(u))\}$ only where denominators are positive. Greenwood is a first-order asymptotic variance estimate, not an exact finite-sample identity. Under independent censoring and finite event-time support, prove consistency by risk-set probabilities and induction at event times, only through horizons with positive event-survival and censoring-survival probabilities. For continuous time, state the pointwise influence expansion $\sqrt n(\hat S(t)-S(t))=n^{-1/2}\sum_i\phi_i(t)+o_P(1)$, $\phi_i(t)=-S(t)\int_0^t s_0(u)^{-1}dM_i(u)$, $s_0(u)=E[Y_i(u)]>0$, and require a proved random-risk-set remainder plus square-integrability before SME-31 applies. No process bands. **B:** hand risk set/support loss. **Requires:** SME-28/30/31; MSF-02 statistic/estimator definition and MSF-14 pointwise delta. **Sources:** Stanford Units 3 pp.1–12 and 12 pp.2–14; Yu pp.30–38 finite-support proof; NIST pp.103–104. Functional proof not read.

pairs.title: Cox PH and partial likelihood
findings_and_repairs: Required an absolutely continuous baseline cumulative hazard to match the displayed density lambda0(t) dt information integral.
pairs.proposal_text_verbatim: **Pages:** cox-ph-and-partial-likelihood / cox-ph-and-partial-likelihood-examples. **A:** Define a Cox model by conditional event intensity $Y_i(t)\lambda_0(t)e^{\beta_0^TZ_i(t)}$ on $[0,\tau]$, with predictable covariates, absolutely continuous baseline cumulative hazard $\Lambda_0(t)=\int_0^t\lambda_0(u)\,du$ with nonnegative integrable hazard density $\lambda_0$, conditional independent censoring and no tied failures for the displayed partial likelihood. Define hazard ratio $e^{\beta^T(z-z')}$, not a risk ratio. Let $R(t)=\{j:U_j\ge t\}$ and give the no-tie partial likelihood $\prod_{i:\delta_i=1}e^{\beta^TZ_i(U_i)}/\sum_{j\in R(U_i)}e^{\beta^TZ_j(U_i)}$; state exact tied-event likelihood separately from Breslow/Efron approximations. For iid independent subjects, fixed dimension, bounded covariates, positive risk denominators on $[0,\tau]$, nonsingular limiting information, correct PH model and a consistent score root, set $s^{(r)}(t)=E[Y_i(t)Z_i(t)^{\otimes r}e^{\beta_0^TZ_i(t)}]$, $\bar z=s^{(1)}/s^{(0)}$, and $I=\int_0^\tau\{s^{(2)}-s^{(1)}s^{(1)T}/s^{(0)}\}\lambda_0(t)\,dt\succ0$. Prove $\sqrt n(\hat\beta-\beta_0)=I^{-1}n^{-1/2}\sum_i\int_0^\tau(Z_i-\bar z(t))\,dM_i(t)+o_P(1)$. Establish uniform risk-set convergence, Hessian convergence to $-I$, square-integrability and negligible random-$\bar Z_n$ replacement before invoking SME-31. No generic MSF-15 Cox result. **B:** risk-set likelihood/time-varying hazard ratio. **Requires:** SME-28/30/31; MSF-01/02; MSF-20 GC only if its exact hypotheses are verified. **Sources:** Stanford Units 5 pp.1–14,23; 7 pp.1–16; 15 pp.1–12; 16 pp.1–8; Yu pp.58–63 discrete-time caveat. pairs.title: Competing risks and cumulative incidence
findings_and_repairs: Pair contract reviewed; exact claims, prerequisites, source ranges and proof obligations are transcribed below.
pairs.proposal_text_verbatim: **Pages:** competing-risks-and-cumulative-incidence / competing-risks-and-cumulative-incidence-examples. **A:** Define observed failure time $T=\min_kT_k$, cause $D=\arg\min_kT_k$ (state no simultaneous causes or an explicit tie rule), all-cause survival $S(t)=P(T>t)$, cause-specific hazard measure by $d\Lambda_k(u)=P(T\in du,D=k\mid T\ge u)$, and cumulative incidence $F_k(t)=P(T\le t,D=k)$. Prove $F_k(t)=\int_{[0,t]}S(u-)\,d\Lambda_k(u)$; in the absolutely continuous case $d\Lambda_k(u)=\lambda_k(u)du$, this is $\int_0^tS(u)\lambda_k(u)\,du$. Define Aalen–Johansen by $\hat S(t)=\prod_{u\le t}(1-\sum_kdN_k(u)/Y(u))$ and $\hat F_k(t)=\sum_{u\le t}\hat S(u-)dN_k(u)/Y(u)$, with risk-set support stated. This is an estimator definition, not a limit theorem here. Latent joint failure times are not identified from the observed first cause without added assumptions; treating other causes as censored does not make $1-\hat S_k$ the observed cause-$k$ CIF. **B:** competing mortality alters cause CIF. **Requires:** SME-28/30/32; MSF-01/02; counting-process and product-limit clauses. **Sources:** Stanford competing-risk slides pp.2–12 only; no second full source, so no variance/process limit.

pairs.title: Calibration and measurement uncertainty
findings_and_repairs: Pair contract reviewed; exact claims, prerequisites, source ranges and proof obligations are transcribed below.
pairs.proposal_text_verbatim: **Pages:** measurement-calibration-and-uncertainty / measurement-calibration-and-uncertainty-examples. **A:** Define measurand $q=f(x_1,\ldots,x_d)$, measured input estimates $\hat x$, corrections/reference standards, and input covariance matrix $\Sigma$. Type A denotes evaluation by statistical analysis of repeated observations; Type B denotes evaluation by other information, not random-versus-systematic error categories. For differentiable $f$ near the input estimate, define first-order combined standard uncertainty by $u_c^2=\nabla f(\hat x)^T\Sigma\nabla f(\hat x)$, explicitly an approximation obtained by Taylor linearization. Include covariance and calibration/reference uncertainty; a later reading of a calibrated instrument may add new repeatability uncertainty. This quantity is not automatically a confidence interval or coverage statement. **B:** calibration curve with uncertain reference standards and batch drift. **Requires:** SME-01; published covariance/Taylor clauses; MSF-14 only if an asymptotic statistical delta limit is claimed. **Sources:** GUM main clauses 1–8 PDF pp.13–39/printed 1–27, full 2026 amendment pp.1–5; NIST process pp.49–85,208–238,243–283. Monte Carlo excluded.

audited_existing_suppliers.current_item_clause_excerpt_verbatim:
Let $X$ be a real random variable on a probability space.

- For $p>0$, the **$p$th absolute moment** of $X$ exists when $|X|^p$ is
  integrable, and is then
  $$\mathbb E[|X|^p].$$
- If $X$ is integrable, its **mean** is $\mathbb E[X]$.
- If $X$ is square-integrable, its **variance** is
  $$\operatorname{Var}(X):=\mathbb E[(X-\mathbb E[X])^2].$$

If $X$ and $Y$ are square-integrable real random variables on the same
probability space, their **covariance** is
$$\operatorname{Cov}(X,Y):=\mathbb E[(X-\mathbb E[X])(Y-\mathbb E[Y])].$$

Then
$$\operatorname{Var}(X)=\mathbb E[X^2]-\mathbb E[X]^2,$$

On finite full-power-set probability spaces these formulas reduce to the
published finite identities.

pairs.title: Detection and quantification limits
findings_and_repairs: Pair contract reviewed; exact claims, prerequisites, source ranges and proof obligations are transcribed below.
pairs.proposal_text_verbatim: **Pages:** detection-and-quantification-limits / detection-and-quantification-limits-examples. **A:** Define $L_C$ as a decision threshold whose blank false-positive probability is $\alpha$, $L_D$ as the concentration giving false-negative probability $\beta$ under the specified signal/blank law, and $L_Q$ as the concentration meeting a declared precision criterion. In the NIST known-blank model with blank $N(0,\sigma_0^2)$, signal $N(c,\sigma_0^2)$, $\alpha=\beta=.05$, and $CV\le k_Q=.10$, derive $L_C=z_{.95}\sigma_0\approx1.645\sigma_0$, $L_D=(z_{.95}+z_{.95})\sigma_0\approx3.29\sigma_0$, and $L_Q=\sigma_0/k_Q=10\sigma_0$, conditional on the equal-known-variance normal model. Estimated blank, heteroscedasticity or a different precision criterion changes the calculation. Below-limit observations are censored measurements and require a measurement likelihood/model. **B:** known/estimated blank, heteroscedasticity. **Requires:** published normal/CDF definitions; MSF-08/10 only for an explicitly calibrated decision/interval. **Sources:** NIST SP958 PDF pp.177–179/printed 164–166. Official Currie PDF HTTP 403; not read.
pairs.exact_supplier_clause: published normal/CDF definitions; MSF-08/10 only for an explicitly calibrated decision/interval.

audited_existing_suppliers.reusable_clause_exact: Scalar normal laws and density normalization; the normal-law definition is homed here rather than on the CLT page. Positive variance is required for exact Student/F denominators.
audited_existing_suppliers.current_item_clause_excerpt_verbatim: Assume AC. Define $\gamma(E)=\int_E e^{-x^2/2}/\sqrt{2\pi}\,dx$ for Borel E in $\mathbb R$. By [[lem-normal-density-has-total-mass-one]] and [[thm-indefinite-integral-of-a-nonnegative-function-is-a-measure]], gamma is a probability measure; denote it $N(0,1)$. For $m\in\mathbb R$ and $\sigma\ge0$, define $N(m,\sigma^2)$ as the law of $x\mapsto m+\sigma x$ on $(\mathbb R,\mathcal B,\gamma)$. This affine map is continuous: for $\sigma$>0 choose $\delta$=$\varepsilon$/$\sigma$, and for $\sigma$=0 it is constant. Its inverse images of opens are open, so it is Borel measurable. [[lem-law-of-a-random-element-is-a-probability-measure]] makes its pushforward a probability. When $\sigma$=0, the preimage of E is all of R if m belongs to E and empty otherwise, so $N(m,0)=\delta_m$ in [[def-dirac-measure]].

pairs.title: Stationary means and sample autocovariance
findings_and_repairs: Pair contract reviewed; exact claims, prerequisites, source ranges and proof obligations are transcribed below.
pairs.proposal_text_verbatim: **Pages:** stationary-time-series-moments-and-autocovariance / stationary-time-series-moments-and-autocovariance-examples. **A:** A process is strictly stationary when all finite-dimensional laws are invariant under time shifts; it is weakly stationary when $E|X_t|^2<\infty$, the mean is constant, and $\gamma(h)=\operatorname{Cov}(X_{t+h},X_t)$ depends only on lag. For weak stationarity prove $\operatorname{Var}(\bar X_n)=n^{-2}\sum_{|h|<n}(n-|h|)\gamma(h)$. If $\sum_{h\in\mathbb Z}|\gamma(h)|<\infty$, derive $\operatorname{Var}(\bar X_n)=O(n^{-1})$ and $L^2$ consistency for the mean; no mixing or CLT follows. Define the biased sample ACVF $\hat\gamma_n(h)=n^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^{n-|h|}(X_t-\bar X_n)(X_{t+|h|}-\bar X_n)$, symmetrically for negative $h$; zero extension makes its Toeplitz quadratic forms nonnegative. The $1/(n-|h|)$ rescaling need not be positive semidefinite. Birkhoff supplies a separate almost-sure/L1 result only under strict stationarity, ergodicity and integrability. **B:** uncorrelated dependent data and indefinite rescaling. **Requires:** SME-01; published covariance identities; Birkhoff only when its exact hypotheses are met. **Sources:** ETH notes full pp.1–57, esp.2–9,13–14; Wang §§2.1–5.7 pp.14–89, Thms.2.2–2.3/Lemma 2.3 p.47. Wang CLT is not used.

audited_existing_suppliers.current_item_clause_excerpt_verbatim:
Let $X$ be a real random variable on a probability space.

- For $p>0$, the **$p$th absolute moment** of $X$ exists when $|X|^p$ is
  integrable, and is then
  $$\mathbb E[|X|^p].$$
- If $X$ is integrable, its **mean** is $\mathbb E[X]$.
- If $X$ is square-integrable, its **variance** is
  $$\operatorname{Var}(X):=\mathbb E[(X-\mathbb E[X])^2].$$

If $X$ and $Y$ are square-integrable real random variables on the same
probability space, their **covariance** is
$$\operatorname{Cov}(X,Y):=\mathbb E[(X-\mathbb E[X])(Y-\mathbb E[Y])].$$

audited_existing_suppliers.current_item_clause_excerpt_verbatim:
Let $S\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$ with Borel sigma-algebra $\mathcal E$, let $(\Omega,\mathcal F,\mathbb P)$ be a
probability space, and let $Y=(Y_n)_{n\ge0}$ be a stochastic process with each
$Y_n:\Omega\to S$ a random element
([[def-stochastic-process-and-finite-dimensional-distributions]]). The process
$Y$ is **strictly stationary** when every finite-dimensional law is unchanged
by a common nonnegative time shift: for every $r\ge1$, every
$0\le n_1<\cdots<n_r$ and every $m\ge0$,

$$\mathcal L(Y_{m+n_1},\ldots,Y_{m+n_r})=\mathcal L(Y_{n_1},\ldots,Y_{n_r}).$$

The **canonical path law** of $Y$ is the pushforward
$\mathbb P_Y=\mathcal L(Y)$ of $\mathbb P$ under the coordinate map
$\omega\mapsto(Y_n(\omega))_{n\ge0}$, a probability measure on the product
space $S^{\mathbb N_0}$ with its product sigma-algebra. The **left shift** is
$\theta(z)_n=z_{n+1}$ for $z=(z_n)_{n\ge0}\in S^{\mathbb N_0}$.

A strictly stationary process is called **ergodic** when the canonical shift $\theta$ is ergodic
for $\mathbb P_Y$ in the sense of
[[def-ergodic-measure-preserving-system]]. The shift-invariance needed for that
definition, namely that $\theta$ is measure preserving for $\mathbb P_Y$, is
proved below for strictly stationary $Y$, so in that case
$(S^{\mathbb N_0},\mathcal E^{\otimes\mathbb N_0},\mathbb P_Y,\theta)$ is a
probability measure-preserving system in the sense of
[[def-measure-preserving-transformation-and-system]].

Let $X,Y$ be square-integrable real random variables on one probability space.
Then
$$\operatorname{Var}(X)=\mathbb E[X^2]-\mathbb E[X]^2,$$
$$\operatorname{Cov}(X,Y)=\mathbb E[XY]-\mathbb E[X]\mathbb E[Y].$$
Moreover, covariance is symmetric and bilinear on finite linear combinations.
On finite full-power-set probability spaces these formulas reduce to the
published finite identities.

audited_existing_suppliers.current_item_clause_excerpt_verbatim:
Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $Y=(Y_n)_{n\ge0}$ be a real-valued
strictly stationary process with $\mathbb E|Y_0|<\infty$
([[def-stationary-process-and-canonical-shift]]), with canonical path law
$\mathbb P_Y$ and left shift $\theta$. Let
$\mathcal I=\{A:\theta^{-1}A=A\}$ be the strictly invariant sigma-algebra on
path space ([[def-strict-and-mod-null-invariant-sigma-algebras]]). Then

$$\frac1n\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}Y_k\ \longrightarrow\ \mathbb E_{\mathbb P_Y}[z_0\mid\mathcal I]\circ\Phi \qquad\text{almost surely and in }L^1(\mathbb P),$$

where $\Phi(\omega)=(Y_n(\omega))_{n\ge0}$ and the conditional expectation is
that of [[def-conditional-expectation-given-a-sigma-algebra]]. If moreover the
canonical shift is ergodic ([[def-ergodic-measure-preserving-system]]), then
the limit is the constant $\mathbb EY_0$. For complex-valued processes the
assertions hold componentwise for real and imaginary parts.

pairs.title: Spectral measures and periodogram bias
findings_and_repairs: Pair contract reviewed; exact claims, prerequisites, source ranges and proof obligations are transcribed below.
pairs.proposal_text_verbatim: **Pages:** spectral-measures-and-periodogram-bias / spectral-measures-and-periodogram-bias-examples. **A:** For weakly stationary $X_t$ on $\mathbb Z$, positive-definiteness of $\gamma$ and the LCA Bochner theorem give a unique finite positive spectral measure $F$ on the circle with $\gamma(h)=\int e^{ih\lambda}F(d\lambda)$. The theorem's continuity/AC+DC hypotheses must be carried; a spectral density exists only if $F\ll d\lambda$, and $\sum_h|\gamma(h)|<\infty$ gives $f(\lambda)=(2\pi)^{-1}\sum_h\gamma(h)e^{-ih\lambda}$ under the declared frequency convention. Define, for known mean, $I_n(\lambda)=(2\pi n)^{-1}|\sum_{t=1}^n(X_t-\mu)e^{-it\lambda}|^2$. Expanding the finite square proves $E I_n$ is Fejér-kernel convolution of $F$ (or $f$ when it exists). For a nonnegative normalized smoothing kernel on the circle, bandwidth $b_n\to0$, $nb_n\to\infty$, and $f$ continuous at the target frequency, prove the approximate-identity bias limit. No raw-periodogram CLT or interval coverage. **B:** atomic sinusoid versus AR(1). **Requires:** SME-40; existing thm-bochner-theorem-for-lca-groups and Fourier convention (AC+DC). **Sources:** Wang Thm.4.2/Cor.4.2 p.63; ETH pp.36–44; Spodarev 2024 pp.16–25/Lemma 2.10.

audited_existing_suppliers.current_item_clause_excerpt_verbatim:
Let $G$ be an abelian group written additively ([[def-group]]) and let
$\phi:G\to\mathbb C$ be a function ([[def-complex-numbers-and-arithmetic]]).
Then $\phi$ is **positive definite** when for every integer $n\ge0$, every
finite family $x_1,\dots,x_n\in G$ and all coefficients
$c_1,\dots,c_n\in\mathbb C$ one has
$$\sum_{j=1}^{n}\sum_{k=1}^{n}c_j\overline{c_k}\,\phi(x_j-x_k)\ \ge\ 0 .$$
The sum for $n=0$ is the empty sum $0$, so the convention covers it; repeated
points $x_j=x_k$ are allowed, so the finite matrices tested are the Hermitian
matrices $[\phi(x_j-x_k)]_{j,k}$. No continuity, boundedness or measurability
is part of the definition.

**Elementary consequences.** The claims below are immediate from the defining
inequality and are recorded here for later use. Taking $n=1$, $x_1=0$ and
$c_1=1$ gives $\phi(0)\ge0$. Taking $n=2$, $x_1=0$, $x_2=x$ and
$c_1=1$, $c_2=t$ gives
$$(1+|t|^2)\phi(0)+\overline{t}\,\phi(-x)+t\,\phi(x)\ \ge\ 0\qquad\text{for every }t\in\mathbb C .$$
The left side is real and equal to its own conjugate for every $t$, so
comparing coefficients at $t=1$ and $t=i$ gives $\phi(-x)=\overline{\phi(x)}$
([[lem-complex-conjugation-and-modulus-laws]]); hence every tested matrix is
Hermitian. If $\phi(x)\ne0$, choose $t=-\overline{\phi(x)}/|\phi(x)|$, so $|t|=1$ and $t\phi(x)=-|\phi(x)|$. The inequality becomes $2\phi(0)-2|\phi(x)|\ge0$, hence $|\phi(x)|\le\phi(0)$; if $\phi(x)=0$, the same bound follows from $\phi(0)\ge0$. Thus a positive definite $\phi$ satisfies
$\phi(0)\ge0$, $\phi(x)=\overline{\phi(-x)}$ and $|\phi(x)|\le\phi(0)$ for all
$x\in G$.

audited_existing_suppliers.current_item_clause_excerpt_verbatim:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Dependent Choice. Let $G$ be a locally compact Hausdorff abelian group with dual $\widehat G$. A continuous function $\phi:G\to\mathbb C$ is positive definite if and only if there is a unique finite positive Radon measure $\mu$ on $\widehat G$ with
$$\phi(x)=\int_{\widehat G}\gamma(x)\,d\mu(\gamma)\qquad(x\in G),$$
and then $\mu(\widehat G)=\phi(0)$. The measure is called the representing measure of $\phi$.

pairs.title: ARMA roots, spectra and inference
findings_and_repairs: Corrected the source’s printed converse typo and excluded its incorrect ARMA root claim.

Kept the existing two iid-innovation inference contracts as explicit additional local result plans; audited the named published ergodic, iid SLLN, scalar/martingale CLT and Cramér–Wold suppliers. These are proposed designs with unresolved complete proof obligations, not completed proofs or generic consequences of stationarity/white noise.
pairs.proposal_text_verbatim:
**Pages:** arma-causality-invertibility-and-spectra / arma-causality-invertibility-and-spectra-examples. **A:** Define ARMA(p,q) by $\phi(B)(X_t-\mu)=\theta(B)\epsilon_t$, $\phi(z)=1-\sum_{j=1}^p\phi_jz^j$, $\theta(z)=1+\sum_{j=1}^q\theta_jz^j$; white noise means centered, finite positive variance and zero covariance at nonzero lags, not iid. Require normalized coprime $\phi,\theta$ after common-factor cancellation. Causal representation with absolutely summable coefficients exists iff $\phi$ has no zero in $|z|\le1$; invertible representation iff $\theta$ has no zero there. A stationary ARMA solution with $\phi\ne0$ on the unit circle has spectral density $f(\lambda)=\sigma^2(2\pi)^{-1}|\theta(e^{-i\lambda})|^2/|\phi(e^{-i\lambda})|^2$, whether or not the displayed representation is causal/invertible. **B:** common factor, unit root, dependent white noise. **Requires:** SME-40/41; existing Cramer–Wold/CLT only for the separate iid-innovation inference clauses (AC). **Sources:** Wang Thms.3.1–3.2 pp.52–55, Thm.4.4 pp.65–66; ETH pp.14–34. Correct printed converse typo; exclude Thm.2.6's incorrect root claim.


**Additional planned inference contracts, proved locally from existing suppliers.** These strengthen the methods for specific iid-innovation models; they are not generic consequences of weak stationarity or white noise. Assume AC as inherited from the probability suppliers.

- `thm-stable-linear-process-sample-mean-clt`: for $X_t-\mu=\sum_{j\ge0}\psi_j\varepsilon_{t-j}$, two-sided iid centered innovations with $0<\sigma^2=E\varepsilon_0^2<\infty$, and $\sum_j\sqrt{j+1}|\psi_j|<\infty$, define $\Psi=\sum_j\psi_j$. Then $\sqrt n(\bar X_n-\mu)\Rightarrow N(0,\sigma^2\Psi^2)$. Causal stable ARMA coefficients decay exponentially and meet the summability premise. Prove existence of the series by Tonelli/L2, and write $\sum_{t=1}^n(X_t-\mu)=\Psi\sum_{t=1}^n\varepsilon_t+R_n$. Minkowski gives $\|R_n\|_2\le\sigma\sum_j|\psi_j|\sqrt{2j}$, hence $R_n/\sqrt n\to0$ in L2; use `thm-lindeberg-levy-iid-central-limit-theorem` and MSF-12. If $\sigma^2\Psi^2>0$ and a variance estimator is proved consistent, Slutsky yields the standardized normal limit and asymptotic interval coverage. Do not imply a variance estimator is consistent merely by naming it, or standardize the zero-variance case.
- `thm-fixed-order-autoregressive-ols-martingale-limit`: for fixed p, a strictly stationary ergodic AR(p) solution $X_t=\phi^TY_t+\varepsilon_t$, $Y_t=(X_{t-1},\ldots,X_{t-p})$, with iid centered innovations independent of the past, $0<\sigma^2<\infty$, and $\Gamma=E[Y_tY_t^T]$ finite positive definite, OLS has $\sqrt n(\hat\phi_n-\phi)\Rightarrow N_p(0,\sigma^2\Gamma^{-1})$. Define a measurable fallback on singular sample Gram matrices and prove its probability tends to zero. Ergodicity gives sample Gram convergence. For each nonzero a, the normalized array $a^TY_t\varepsilon_t/\sqrt{n\sigma^2a^T\Gamma a}$, padded by zeros after n, has predictable variance clock tending to one. Its **unconditional** Lindeberg sum tends to zero by dominated convergence and finite $E[(a^TY_t\varepsilon_t)^2]$, exactly matching the existing `thm-martingale-central-limit-theorem`. Apply `thm-cramer-wold-device`, then MSF-12 and continuity of matrix inversion. The residual mean-square estimator of $\sigma^2$ is consistent by expanding the residual square, the innovation SLLN and Gram convergence; this supplies plug-in fixed-order Wald calibration. Do not condition on the entire lag-design matrix as if it were a fixed exogenous design, or infer validity after data-selected order. The same argument applies with a predictable constant intercept added to Y and with the corresponding parameter dimension and positive-definite Gram matrix. For stable AR(p) with unknown mean, this supplies a fitted innovation variance and slope vector; prove that $\hat\tau^2=\hat\sigma^2/(1-\sum_j\hat\phi_j)^2$ is consistent by continuity and the nonzero stable-model denominator. This gives an actual plug-in long-run variance for the preceding mean interval, without assuming a generic HAC estimator or later computational statistics.

The existing `thm-stationary-process-birkhoff-ergodic-limit`, `thm-kolmogorov-iid-l1-strong-law`, scalar iid/martingale CLTs and `thm-cramer-wold-device` are actual local prerequisite bodies for these routes. Their hypotheses and AC convention were checked. These are planned local proof obligations, not completed item proofs or claims that the source notes supplied these exact arguments. No generic ACVF/periodogram or mixing-process CLT is introduced.

where $\Phi(\omega)=(Y_n(\omega))_{n\ge0}$ and the conditional expectation is
that of [[def-conditional-expectation-given-a-sigma-algebra]]. If moreover the
canonical shift is ergodic ([[def-ergodic-measure-preserving-system]]), then
the limit is the constant $\mathbb EY_0$. For complex-valued processes the
assertions hold componentwise for real and imaginary parts.

proof_route_clauses_verbatim: - `thm-stable-linear-process-sample-mean-clt`: for $X_t-\mu=\sum_{j\ge0}\psi_j\varepsilon_{t-j}$, two-sided iid centered innovations with $0<\sigma^2=E\varepsilon_0^2<\infty$, and $\sum_j\sqrt{j+1}|\psi_j|<\infty$, define $\Psi=\sum_j\psi_j$. Then $\sqrt n(\bar X_n-\mu)\Rightarrow N(0,\sigma^2\Psi^2)$. Causal stable ARMA coefficients decay exponentially and meet the summability premise. Prove existence of the series by Tonelli/L2, and write $\sum_{t=1}^n(X_t-\mu)=\Psi\sum_{t=1}^n\varepsilon_t+R_n$. Minkowski gives $\|R_n\|_2\le\sigma\sum_j|\psi_j|\sqrt{2j}$, hence $R_n/\sqrt n\to0$ in L2; use `thm-lindeberg-levy-iid-central-limit-theorem` and MSF-12. If $\sigma^2\Psi^2>0$ and a variance estimator is proved consistent, Slutsky yields the standardized normal limit and asymptotic interval coverage. Do not imply a variance estimator is consistent merely by naming it, or standardize the zero-variance case.

- `thm-fixed-order-autoregressive-ols-martingale-limit`: for fixed p, a strictly stationary ergodic AR(p) solution $X_t=\phi^TY_t+\varepsilon_t$, $Y_t=(X_{t-1},\ldots,X_{t-p})$, with iid centered innovations independent of the past, $0<\sigma^2<\infty$, and $\Gamma=E[Y_tY_t^T]$ finite positive definite, OLS has $\sqrt n(\hat\phi_n-\phi)\Rightarrow N_p(0,\sigma^2\Gamma^{-1})$. Define a measurable fallback on singular sample Gram matrices and prove its probability tends to zero. Ergodicity gives sample Gram convergence. For each nonzero a, the normalized array $a^TY_t\varepsilon_t/\sqrt{n\sigma^2a^T\Gamma a}$, padded by zeros after n, has predictable variance clock tending to one. Its **unconditional** Lindeberg sum tends to zero by dominated convergence and finite $E[(a^TY_t\varepsilon_t)^2]$, exactly matching the existing `thm-martingale-central-limit-theorem`. Apply `thm-cramer-wold-device`, then MSF-12 and continuity of matrix inversion. The residual mean-square estimator of $\sigma^2$ is consistent by expanding the residual square, the innovation SLLN and Gram convergence; this supplies plug-in fixed-order Wald calibration. Do not condition on the entire lag-design matrix as if it were a fixed exogenous design, or infer validity after data-selected order. The same argument applies with a predictable constant intercept added to Y and with the corresponding parameter dimension and positive-definite Gram matrix. For stable AR(p) with unknown mean, this supplies a fitted innovation variance and slope vector; prove that $\hat\tau^2=\hat\sigma^2/(1-\sum_j\hat\phi_j)^2$ is consistent by continuity and the nonzero stable-model denominator. This gives an actual plug-in long-run variance for the preceding mean interval, without assuming a generic HAC estimator or later computational statistics.

Require normalized coprime $\phi,\theta$ after common-factor cancellation. Causal representation with absolutely summable coefficients exists iff $\phi$ has no zero in $|z|\le1$; invertible representation iff $\theta$ has no zero there. A stationary ARMA solution with $\phi\ne0$ on the unit circle has spectral density $f(\lambda)=\sigma^2(2\pi)^{-1}|\theta(e^{-i\lambda})|^2/|\phi(e^{-i\lambda})|^2$, whether or not the displayed representation is causal/invertible. **B:** common factor, unit root, dependent white noise.

findings_and_repairs: Pair contract reviewed; exact claims, prerequisites, source ranges and proof obligations are transcribed below.
pairs.proposal_text_verbatim: **Pages:** linear-prediction-for-dependent-data / linear-prediction-for-dependent-data-examples. **A:** For weakly stationary $X_t\in L^2$, define the finite-history predictor of $X_{n+h}$ as the $L^2$ projection onto $\operatorname{span}\{1,X_1,\ldots,X_n\}$. The existing affine L2 theorem supplies a unique predictor class even if coefficients are nonunique. If centered history covariance $\Gamma$ is nonsingular, derive $\Gamma a=\gamma_h$, intercept $\mu(1-\sum_i a_i)$, and projection error variance $\gamma(0)-a^T\gamma_h$ for the corresponding stationary lag vector. If $\Gamma$ is singular, state only the unique predictor class/minimizer set from the supplier. Joint Gaussianity makes the projection equal $E[X_{n+h}\mid X_1,\ldots,X_n]$; otherwise conditional expectation may be nonlinear. Optional Durbin–Levinson is a procedure with covariance input, initialization and updates; separately prove by induction that it solves successive Toeplitz systems and returns projection-error variances, requiring positive-definite leading blocks. **B:** singular covariance/Gaussian contrast. **Requires:** SME-40; existing thm-normal-equations-for-best-affine-l2-prediction. **Sources:** Wang §5 pp.67–75; Dewei notes; existing supplier resolves incomplete uniqueness exercise.

audited_existing_suppliers.reusable_clause_exact: Measurable observations/laws, expectation and indicator linearity, finite moments/covariance and affine L2 projection. Predictor class is unique even if coefficients are not. No sampling-design or model-specific inference theorem.
audited_existing_suppliers.current_item_clause_excerpt_verbatim:
Let $X,Y_1,\dots,Y_n$ be square-integrable real random variables on one
probability space, and write
$$W:=\operatorname{span}\big([1],[Y_1],\dots,[Y_n]\big)\subseteq L^2(\mathbb P),$$
where $[\cdot]$ denotes the almost-everywhere class from
[[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]].

Then there is a unique class $[Z_*]\in W$ minimizing $\|[X]-[Z]\|_2$ over
$[Z]\in W$. This minimizing class has an affine representative
$Z_*=a_0+\sum_{j=1}^n a_jY_j$, and its coefficients satisfy
$$a_0=\mathbb E[X]-\sum_{j=1}^n a_j\mathbb E[Y_j],$$
$$\sum_{j=1}^n \operatorname{Cov}(Y_i,Y_j)a_j=\operatorname{Cov}(X,Y_i)\qquad(1\le i\le n).$$

The class $[Z_*]$ is unique. If the covariance matrix
$\Gamma=(\operatorname{Cov}(Y_i,Y_j))_{i,j}$ is singular, the coefficient vector
need not be uniquely determined by the normal equations, but any two solutions
yield the same predictor almost surely.

pairs.proposal_text_verbatim: **Pages:** state-space-models-as-probability-laws / state-space-models-as-probability-laws-examples. **A:** For finite horizon $T$, define standard-Borel state spaces $E_0,\ldots,E_T$, observation spaces $F_1,\ldots,F_T$, initial law $\mu_0$, jointly measurable transition probability kernels $K_t(x_{t-1},dx_t)$, and jointly measurable observation kernels $G_t(x_t,dy_t)$. Separately define the linear-Gaussian subclass $x_0\sim N(m_0,P_0)$, $x_t=F_tx_{t-1}+q_t$, $y_t=H_tx_t+r_t$, where $q_t\sim N(0,Q_t)$, $r_t\sim N(0,R_t)$, all noises are centered and mutually independent across times and from $x_0$, and $P_0,Q_t,R_t$ are positive semidefinite. pairs.title: Random fields and variograms
findings_and_repairs: Restricted the displacement-only variogram to order-two intrinsic stationarity before proving conditional negative definiteness.
pairs.proposal_text_verbatim: **Pages:** random-fields-covariance-and-variograms / random-fields-covariance-and-variograms-examples. **A:** Define a real random field as $(X(s))_{s\in T}$ on $T\subseteq\mathbb R^d$; separately state coordinate measurability and joint measurability when spatial integration is used. Define strict stationarity by shift-invariant finite-dimensional laws, wide stationarity by constant mean and covariance $C(s,t)=C(t-s)$, isotropy by dependence only on $\|t-s\|$, and order-two intrinsic stationarity by stationary increments with finite second moments. A covariance kernel is positive semidefinite by the variance of every finite linear combination. Given a symmetric positive-semidefinite kernel and mean, consistent Gaussian finite-dimensional laws plus Kolmogorov extension give a field on the cylinder sigma-algebra, not continuous sample paths; both Gaussian and extension suppliers carry AC. For an order-two intrinsically stationary field, define the displacement-only variogram $\gamma(h)=\tfrac12E[(X(s+h)-X(s))^2]$, which is independent of $s$; under wide stationarity $\gamma(h)=C(0)-C(h)$. Prove conditional negative definiteness: for real $a_i$ with $\sum_i a_i=0$, $\sum_{i,j}a_ia_j\gamma(s_i-s_j)\le0$, by expanding the variance of the corresponding finite combination of increments. Bochner representation requires continuous covariance and inherits AC+DC; omit Schoenberg's converse. **B:** invalid $C(h)=1+h^2$, valid $\gamma(h)=h^2$. **Requires:** SME-40/41; published multivariate-normal, FDD, Kolmogorov and LCA Bochner items (AC for Gaussian/Kolmogorov; AC+DC for Bochner). **Sources:** Spodarev 2024 §§1.1–1.2 pp.3–8; 2009 §§1.3–1.4 pp.14–20, Thm.2.1.1 p.35, Prop.2.2.1 pp.43–46. Use real coefficients to fix printed complex-weight issue.

Let $G$ be an abelian group written additively ([[def-group]]) and let
$\phi:G\to\mathbb C$ be a function ([[def-complex-numbers-and-arithmetic]]).
Then $\phi$ is **positive definite** when for every integer $n\ge0$, every
finite family $x_1,\dots,x_n\in G$ and all coefficients
$c_1,\dots,c_n\in\mathbb C$ one has
$$\sum_{j=1}^{n}\sum_{k=1}^{n}c_j\overline{c_k}\,\phi(x_j-x_k)\ \ge\ 0 .$$
The sum for $n=0$ is the empty sum $0$, so the convention covers it; repeated
points $x_j=x_k$ are allowed, so the finite matrices tested are the Hermitian
matrices $[\phi(x_j-x_k)]_{j,k}$. No continuity, boundedness or measurability
is part of the definition.

**Elementary consequences.** The claims below are immediate from the defining
inequality and are recorded here for later use. Taking $n=1$, $x_1=0$ and
$c_1=1$ gives $\phi(0)\ge0$. Taking $n=2$, $x_1=0$, $x_2=x$ and
$c_1=1$, $c_2=t$ gives
$$(1+|t|^2)\phi(0)+\overline{t}\,\phi(-x)+t\,\phi(x)\ \ge\ 0\qquad\text{for every }t\in\mathbb C .$$
The left side is real and equal to its own conjugate for every $t$, so
comparing coefficients at $t=1$ and $t=i$ gives $\phi(-x)=\overline{\phi(x)}$
([[lem-complex-conjugation-and-modulus-laws]]); hence every tested matrix is
Hermitian. If $\phi(x)\ne0$, choose $t=-\overline{\phi(x)}/|\phi(x)|$, so $|t|=1$ and $t\phi(x)=-|\phi(x)|$. The inequality becomes $2\phi(0)-2|\phi(x)|\ge0$, hence $|\phi(x)|\le\phi(0)$; if $\phi(x)=0$, the same bound follows from $\phi(0)\ge0$. Thus a positive definite $\phi$ satisfies
$\phi(0)\ge0$, $\phi(x)=\overline{\phi(-x)}$ and $|\phi(x)|\le\phi(0)$ for all
$x\in G$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Dependent Choice. Let $G$ be a locally compact Hausdorff abelian group with dual $\widehat G$. A continuous function $\phi:G\to\mathbb C$ is positive definite if and only if there is a unique finite positive Radon measure $\mu$ on $\widehat G$ with

future_proof_authoring_obligations.scope_and_assumptions_clause_verbatim: **Pages:** random-fields-covariance-and-variograms / random-fields-covariance-and-variograms-examples. **A:** Define a real random field as $(X(s))_{s\in T}$ on $T\subseteq\mathbb R^d$; separately state coordinate measurability and joint measurability when spatial integration is used. Define strict stationarity by shift-invariant finite-dimensional laws, wide stationarity by constant mean and covariance $C(s,t)=C(t-s)$, isotropy by dependence only on $\|t-s\|$, and order-two intrinsic stationarity by stationary increments with finite second moments. A covariance kernel is positive semidefinite by the variance of every finite linear combination. Given a symmetric positive-semidefinite kernel and mean, consistent Gaussian finite-dimensional laws plus Kolmogorov extension give a field on the cylinder sigma-algebra, not continuous sample paths; both Gaussian and extension suppliers carry AC. For an order-two intrinsically stationary field, define the displacement-only variogram $\gamma(h)=\tfrac12E[(X(s+h)-X(s))^2]$, which is independent of $s$; under wide stationarity $\gamma(h)=C(0)-C(h)$. Prove conditional negative definiteness: for real $a_i$ with $\sum_i a_i=0$, $\sum_{i,j}a_ia_j\gamma(s_i-s_j)\le0$, by expanding the variance of the corresponding finite combination of increments. Bochner representation requires continuous covariance and inherits AC+DC; omit Schoenberg's converse. **B:** invalid $C(h)=1+h^2$, valid $\gamma(h)=h^2$.

audited_existing_suppliers.current_item_clause_excerpt_verbatim:
Let $X$ be a real random variable on a probability space.

- For $p>0$, the **$p$th absolute moment** of $X$ exists when $|X|^p$ is
  integrable, and is then
  $$\mathbb E[|X|^p].$$
- If $X$ is integrable, its **mean** is $\mathbb E[X]$.
- If $X$ is square-integrable, its **variance** is
  $$\operatorname{Var}(X):=\mathbb E[(X-\mathbb E[X])^2].$$

If $X$ and $Y$ are square-integrable real random variables on the same
probability space, their **covariance** is
$$\operatorname{Cov}(X,Y):=\mathbb E[(X-\mathbb E[X])(Y-\mathbb E[Y])].$$

Let $X,Y$ be square-integrable real random variables on one probability space.
Then
$$\operatorname{Var}(X)=\mathbb E[X^2]-\mathbb E[X]^2,$$
$$\operatorname{Cov}(X,Y)=\mathbb E[XY]-\mathbb E[X]\mathbb E[Y].$$
Moreover, covariance is symmetric and bilinear on finite linear combinations.
On finite full-power-set probability spaces these formulas reduce to the
published finite identities.

pairs.title: Kriging
findings_and_repairs: Pair contract reviewed; exact claims, prerequisites, source ranges and proof obligations are transcribed below.
pairs.proposal_text_verbatim: **Pages:** kriging-as-best-linear-prediction / kriging-as-best-linear-prediction-examples. **A:** For observations $Z=(X(s_1),\ldots,X(s_n))^T$, target $X(s_0)$, covariance matrix $\Sigma$, and covariance vector $c_0$, define simple kriging with known mean $m$ by $\hat X_0=m(s_0)+\lambda^T(Z-m)$. If $\Sigma\succ0$, minimization of mean-square prediction error gives $\lambda=\Sigma^{-1}c_0$ and error variance $C(0)-c_0^T\Sigma^{-1}c_0$. For Gaussian fields with known mean/covariance this is the conditional mean; otherwise it is only the best affine predictor. Ordinary kriging treats an unknown constant mean by imposing $1^T\lambda=1$; universal kriging with trend $p(s)^T\beta$ imposes $P^T\lambda=p(s_0)$, where $P$ is the finite observation-site design matrix. Give the Lagrange/KKT systems and require nonsingular $\Sigma$, full column rank $P$, and the corresponding augmented-system invertibility; for variogram formulations state conditional negative definiteness separately. Plug-in covariance/trend estimates do not retain oracle optimality. **B:** singular covariance, rank failure and ordinary/simple variance difference. **Requires:** SME-43/45; published least-squares/affine projection; MSF-03 only for explicit prediction-risk terminology (AC for Gaussian law). **Sources:** Spodarev 2024 §§3.1–3.2 pp.26–48; Sun Stanford Lecture 5 full. Exclude Lemma 3.28's finite-site rank error.

audited_existing_suppliers.current_item_clause_excerpt_verbatim: Assume AC and let $d\ge1$ be finite. For $m\in\mathbb R^d$ and a real symmetric positive semidefinite matrix $\Sigma$, a Borel probability law is denoted $N_d(m,\Sigma)$ when a vector X with that law satisfies $u\cdot X\sim N(u\cdot m,u^T\Sigma u)$ for every $u\in\mathbb R^d$. Such a law exists, has mean m and covariance Sigma, and can be realized as $m+\Sigma^{1/2}Z$ with independent standard-normal coordinates. Singular Sigma is allowed. Uniqueness will be proved in the following characteristic-function lemma.

Let $T:V\to W$ be a linear map between finite-dimensional inner product spaces and let $b\in W$. A vector $x\in V$ minimises $\lVert Tx-b\rVert$ if and only if

$$T^*(Tx-b)=0,$$

equivalently $T^*Tx=T^*b$. Minimisers exist, and if $x_0$ is one minimiser, then the full set of minimisers is $x_0+\ker T$.

audited_existing_suppliers.current_item_clause_excerpt_verbatim:
Let $X,Y_1,\dots,Y_n$ be square-integrable real random variables on one
probability space, and write
$$W:=\operatorname{span}\big([1],[Y_1],\dots,[Y_n]\big)\subseteq L^2(\mathbb P),$$
where $[\cdot]$ denotes the almost-everywhere class from
[[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]].

Then there is a unique class $[Z_*]\in W$ minimizing $\|[X]-[Z]\|_2$ over
$[Z]\in W$. This minimizing class has an affine representative
$Z_*=a_0+\sum_{j=1}^n a_jY_j$, and its coefficients satisfy
$$a_0=\mathbb E[X]-\sum_{j=1}^n a_j\mathbb E[Y_j],$$
$$\sum_{j=1}^n \operatorname{Cov}(Y_i,Y_j)a_j=\operatorname{Cov}(X,Y_i)\qquad(1\le i\le n).$$

The class $[Z_*]$ is unique. If the covariance matrix
$\Gamma=(\operatorname{Cov}(Y_i,Y_j))_{i,j}$ is singular, the coefficient vector
need not be uniquely determined by the normal equations, but any two solutions
yield the same predictor almost surely.

pairs.title: Poisson and Cox point processes
findings_and_repairs: Added the exact published scalar Poisson mass example as a limited count-law convention supplier; it is not a point-process theorem.
pairs.proposal_text_verbatim:
**Pages:** poisson-and-cox-point-process-models / poisson-and-cox-point-process-models-examples. **A:** On a stated locally compact second-countable Borel space $S$, define a point process as a random locally finite counting measure $\eta$; distinguish simple from multiplicity-bearing processes. Define intensity measure $
u(B)=E\eta(B)$. State the Poisson-process existence theorem for locally finite $\sigma$-finite $
u$, with proof by independent Poisson counts on a countable precompact partition and consistency/extension. A Poisson process has independent counts on disjoint measurable sets with $N(B)\sim\operatorname{Poisson}(
u(B))$; a Cox process is conditionally Poisson given a random directing measure $\xi$, with the conditional law a measurable probability kernel. State Campbell $E\eta(f)=\int f\,d
u$, Poisson Laplace functional $E e^{-\eta(f)}=\exp[-\int(1-e^{-f})d
u]$, and Mecke identity $\displaystyle E\sum_{x\in\eta}h(x,\eta-\delta_x)=\int E[h(x,\eta)]\,
u(dx)$ for measurable $h\ge0$, including the source converse characterization under its sigma-finite/local-finiteness hypotheses. For a Cox process and $\varphi\ge0$, $\eta(\varphi)=\int\varphi\,d\eta$, assume $\varphi\in L^1(
u)\cap L^2(
u)$ and $E[\xi(\varphi)^2]<\infty$; conditioning gives $E[\eta(\varphi)^2]=E[\xi(\varphi^2)+\xi(\varphi)^2]$ and $\operatorname{Var}\eta(\varphi)=
u(\varphi^2)+\operatorname{Var}(\xi(\varphi))$. State the exact equivalence of finite second moments only with these hypotheses. Campbell/Laplace/Mecke proofs use simple functions, monotone convergence and the Poisson count law. Exclude directing-law uniqueness (source's final analytic uniqueness step is externally cited) and diffuse-intensity simplicity unless separately proved. **B:** random/deterministic intensity with the same mean and different count variance. **Requires:** SME-30 only where compensator is used; published measure/kernel/product integration items; no point-process law is supplied by ordinary counting measure. **Sources:** Last–Penrose Chs.1–4 pp.13–49, Ch.13 pp.139–147; Baddeley Lecture 1 pp.1–25. Unread invoked Ch.6 excluded.

audited_existing_suppliers.current_item_clause_excerpt_verbatim:
Let $X$ be a set. The **counting set function** on $\mathcal P(X)$ is

$$\#_X(E):=\begin{cases}|E|,&E\text{ is finite},\\+\infty,&E\text{ is infinite},\end{cases}$$

where finite means equinumerous with a natural number ([[def-countable]]) and $+\infty$ belongs to the extended real line ([[def-extended-reals]]). The two branches are exhaustive and disjoint. The fact that this set function is a measure, and hence deserves the name **counting measure**, is proved in [[prop-counting-measure-is-a-measure]].

audited_existing_suppliers.current_item_clause_excerpt_verbatim:
Let $X$ be a set and let $\mathcal A$ be a sigma-algebra on $X$ ([[def-sigma-algebra]]). A **measure** on $(X,\mathcal A)$ is a function

$$\mu:\mathcal A\longrightarrow[0,+\infty]\subseteq\overline{\mathbb R}$$

such that:

1. $\mu(\varnothing)=0$;
2. for every pairwise disjoint sequence $(E_k)_{k\in\mathbb N}$ in $\mathcal A$,
   $$\mu\left(\bigcup_{k\in\mathbb N}E_k\right)=\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\mu(E_k),$$
   where the right side is the nonnegative extended sum of [[def-nonnegative-extended-series]].

The second condition is **countable additivity**. It begins at index $0$ and includes the case in which some term or the total sum is $+\infty$.

**Pages:** poisson-and-cox-point-process-models / poisson-and-cox-point-process-models-examples. **A:** On a stated locally compact second-countable Borel space $S$, define a point process as a random locally finite counting measure $\eta$; distinguish simple from multiplicity-bearing processes. Define intensity measure $
u(B)=E\eta(B)$. State the Poisson-process existence theorem for locally finite $\sigma$-finite $
u$, with proof by independent Poisson counts on a countable precompact partition and consistency/extension. A Poisson process has independent counts on disjoint measurable sets with $N(B)\sim\operatorname{Poisson}(
u(B))$; a Cox process is conditionally Poisson given a random directing measure $\xi$, with the conditional law a measurable probability kernel. State Campbell $E\eta(f)=\int f\,d
u$, Poisson Laplace functional $E e^{-\eta(f)}=\exp[-\int(1-e^{-f})d
u]$, and Mecke identity $\displaystyle E\sum_{x\in\eta}h(x,\eta-\delta_x)=\int E[h(x,\eta)]\,
u(dx)$ for measurable $h\ge0$, including the source converse characterization under its sigma-finite/local-finiteness hypotheses. For a Cox process and $\varphi\ge0$, $\eta(\varphi)=\int\varphi\,d\eta$, assume $\varphi\in L^1(
u)\cap L^2(
u)$ and $E[\xi(\varphi)^2]<\infty$; conditioning gives $E[\eta(\varphi)^2]=E[\xi(\varphi^2)+\xi(\varphi)^2]$ and $\operatorname{Var}\eta(\varphi)=
u(\varphi^2)+\operatorname{Var}(\xi(\varphi))$. State the exact equivalence of finite second moments only with these hypotheses. Campbell/Laplace/Mecke proofs use simple functions, monotone convergence and the Poisson count law. Exclude directing-law uniqueness (source's final analytic uniqueness step is externally cited) and diffuse-intensity simplicity unless separately proved. **B:** random/deterministic intensity with the same mean and different count variance.

pairs.title: Spatial summaries and Palm laws
findings_and_repairs: Pair contract reviewed; exact claims, prerequisites, source ranges and proof obligations are transcribed below.
pairs.proposal_text_verbatim: **Pages:** spatial-point-process-summaries-and-palm-laws / spatial-point-process-summaries-and-palm-laws-examples. **A:** For a stationary point process $\eta$ on $\mathbb R^d$ with finite positive intensity $\rho$, define the second factorial moment measure $\alpha^{(2)}(A\times B)=E\sum_{x\ne y\in\eta}1_A(x)1_B(y)$, reduced moment measure, and pair-correlation density $g$ only when the required absolute-continuity density exists. Define the Palm law $P^0$ by the refined Campbell identity $E\sum_{x\in\eta}h(x,\eta-\delta_x)=\rho\int_{\mathbb R^d}E^0[h(x,\eta)]\,dx$, not by conditioning on a zero-probability event. Define Ripley's $K(r)=\rho^{-1}E^0[\eta(B(0,r)\setminus\{0\})]$; if the second factorial density is $\rho^2g(u)$, prove $K(r)=\int_{B(0,r)}g(u)\,du$, and for Poisson $K(r)=|B(0,r)|$. Define edge-corrected K estimators as procedures with the correction weight stated, with no automatic unbiasedness claim. For compact convex $W$ with nonempty interior and dilations $W_n=a_nW$, state the Last–Penrose result $\eta(W_n)/|W_n|\to E[\eta(Q)\mid\mathcal I]$ in $L^1$, where $Q$ is a unit-volume reference set and $\mathcal I$ is the translation-invariant sigma-algebra; ergodicity makes the limit $\rho$. No rate/CLT. **B:** edge effects and absent pair-correlation density. **Requires:** SME-48; published measure and ergodic suppliers under their exact conditions. **Sources:** Last–Penrose Ch.8 pp.81–93 Thm.8.14, Ch.9 pp.94–103 Thms.9.1/9.4; Baddeley Lectures 2–3 pp.26–56.

audited_existing_suppliers.current_item_clause_excerpt_verbatim:
Let $X$ be a set. The **counting set function** on $\mathcal P(X)$ is

$$\#_X(E):=\begin{cases}|E|,&E\text{ is finite},\\+\infty,&E\text{ is infinite},\end{cases}$$

where finite means equinumerous with a natural number ([[def-countable]]) and $+\infty$ belongs to the extended real line ([[def-extended-reals]]). The two branches are exhaustive and disjoint. The fact that this set function is a measure, and hence deserves the name **counting measure**, is proved in [[prop-counting-measure-is-a-measure]].

audited_existing_suppliers.current_item_clause_excerpt_verbatim:
Let $X$ be a set and let $\mathcal A$ be a sigma-algebra on $X$ ([[def-sigma-algebra]]). A **measure** on $(X,\mathcal A)$ is a function

$$\mu:\mathcal A\longrightarrow[0,+\infty]\subseteq\overline{\mathbb R}$$

such that:

1. $\mu(\varnothing)=0$;
2. for every pairwise disjoint sequence $(E_k)_{k\in\mathbb N}$ in $\mathcal A$,
   $$\mu\left(\bigcup_{k\in\mathbb N}E_k\right)=\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\mu(E_k),$$
   where the right side is the nonnegative extended sum of [[def-nonnegative-extended-series]].

The second condition is **countable additivity**. It begins at index $0$ and includes the case in which some term or the total sum is $+\infty$.

audited_existing_suppliers.current_item_clause_excerpt_verbatim:
Let $S\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$ with Borel sigma-algebra $\mathcal E$, let $(\Omega,\mathcal F,\mathbb P)$ be a
probability space, and let $Y=(Y_n)_{n\ge0}$ be a stochastic process with each
$Y_n:\Omega\to S$ a random element
([[def-stochastic-process-and-finite-dimensional-distributions]]). The process
$Y$ is **strictly stationary** when every finite-dimensional law is unchanged
by a common nonnegative time shift: for every $r\ge1$, every
$0\le n_1<\cdots<n_r$ and every $m\ge0$,

$$\mathcal L(Y_{m+n_1},\ldots,Y_{m+n_r})=\mathcal L(Y_{n_1},\ldots,Y_{n_r}).$$

The **canonical path law** of $Y$ is the pushforward
$\mathbb P_Y=\mathcal L(Y)$ of $\mathbb P$ under the coordinate map
$\omega\mapsto(Y_n(\omega))_{n\ge0}$, a probability measure on the product
space $S^{\mathbb N_0}$ with its product sigma-algebra. The **left shift** is
$\theta(z)_n=z_{n+1}$ for $z=(z_n)_{n\ge0}\in S^{\mathbb N_0}$.

A strictly stationary process is called **ergodic** when the canonical shift $\theta$ is ergodic
for $\mathbb P_Y$ in the sense of
[[def-ergodic-measure-preserving-system]]. The shift-invariance needed for that
definition, namely that $\theta$ is measure preserving for $\mathbb P_Y$, is
proved below for strictly stationary $Y$, so in that case
$(S^{\mathbb N_0},\mathcal E^{\otimes\mathbb N_0},\mathbb P_Y,\theta)$ is a
probability measure-preserving system in the sense of
[[def-measure-preserving-transformation-and-system]].

audited_existing_suppliers.current_item_clause_excerpt_verbatim:
Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $Y=(Y_n)_{n\ge0}$ be a real-valued
strictly stationary process with $\mathbb E|Y_0|<\infty$
([[def-stationary-process-and-canonical-shift]]), with canonical path law
$\mathbb P_Y$ and left shift $\theta$. Let
$\mathcal I=\{A:\theta^{-1}A=A\}$ be the strictly invariant sigma-algebra on
path space ([[def-strict-and-mod-null-invariant-sigma-algebras]]). Then

$$\frac1n\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}Y_k\ \longrightarrow\ \mathbb E_{\mathbb P_Y}[z_0\mid\mathcal I]\circ\Phi \qquad\text{almost surely and in }L^1(\mathbb P),$$

where $\Phi(\omega)=(Y_n(\omega))_{n\ge0}$ and the conditional expectation is
that of [[def-conditional-expectation-given-a-sigma-algebra]]. If moreover the
canonical shift is ergodic ([[def-ergodic-measure-preserving-system]]), then
the limit is the constant $\mathbb EY_0$. For complex-valued processes the
assertions hold componentwise for real and imaginary parts.

pairs.title: Finite-window spatial likelihood
findings_and_repairs: Pair contract reviewed; exact claims, prerequisites, source ranges and proof obligations are transcribed below.
pairs.proposal_text_verbatim: **Pages:** finite-window-spatial-point-process-likelihoods / finite-window-spatial-point-process-likelihoods-examples. **A:** State bounded observation window $W\subset\mathbb R^d$, reference measure and boundary convention. For a Poisson process with measurable intensity $\lambda_\theta\ge0$ and $\int_W\lambda_\theta(x)dx<\infty$, derive its density relative to unit-rate Poisson measure $P_0$: $dP_\theta/dP_0(\eta)=\exp\{|W|-\int_W\lambda_\theta\}\prod_{x\in\eta\cap W}\lambda_\theta(x)$; hence log likelihood up to a parameter-free constant is $\sum_{x\in\eta\cap W}\log\lambda_\theta(x)-\int_W\lambda_\theta(x)dx$. For homogeneous $\lambda_\rho=\rho\ge0$, if $N(W)>0$, maximize at $\hat\rho=N(W)/|W|$; if $N(W)=0$, the supremum is at $\rho=0$, attained only when the parameter space includes zero. Define finite-window Gibbs density relative to a specified Poisson reference by $Z_\theta^{-1}e^{-H_\theta(\eta)}1_{\{\eta\in\mathcal S_\theta\}}$, requiring support $\mathcal S_\theta$ and $0<Z_\theta<\infty$. Where a Papangelou conditional intensity $\lambda_\theta(u;\eta)$ is defined, define pseudolikelihood as $\prod_{x\in\eta\cap W}\lambda_\theta(x;\eta\setminus\{x\})\exp\{-\int_W\lambda_\theta(u;\eta)\,du\}$, with boundary/exposure convention stated; it is not the joint likelihood and no consistency/asymptotic guarantee is claimed. **B:** Poisson/Strauss exact likelihood versus pseudolikelihood. **Requires:** SME-48; MSF-04 dominated-likelihood definition only for the stated reference-density interpretation. **Sources:** Baddeley Lecture 4 pp.57–73.

pairs.title: Temporal intensity and likelihood
findings_and_repairs: Pair contract reviewed; exact claims, prerequisites, source ranges and proof obligations are transcribed below.
pairs.proposal_text_verbatim: **Pages:** temporal-point-process-intensity-and-likelihood / temporal-point-process-intensity-and-likelihood-examples. **A:** Define simple locally finite ordered event times $0<T_1<T_2<\cdots$, history filtration $\mathcal F_t$, and nonnegative predictable conditional intensity $\lambda^*(t)$ with $\int_0^T\lambda^*(u)du<\infty$ a.s. on each finite window and compensator contract $N(t)-\int_0^t\lambda^*(u)du$ a martingale. Conditional on history at $t$, derive next-event survival $\exp\{-\int_t^u\lambda^*(s\mid\text{no event after }t)ds\}$ and its density where the cumulative hazard is absolutely continuous. For observed event times $t_1<\cdots<t_m\le T$, derive likelihood relative to unit-rate Poisson reference proportional to $\prod_{i=1}^m\lambda^*(t_i)\exp\{-\int_0^T\lambda^*(u)du\}$, with positive event intensity at observed events and the terminal no-event factor included. Finite cumulative hazard to infinity permits a terminal mass at no further event; next-event a.s. requires infinite cumulative hazard and a non-explosion condition. Marked processes require their conditional mark law factor. Intensity specification alone proves neither existence/stationarity of a realization nor Hawkes stability. **B:** Poisson, Hawkes specification with existence kept separate, and terminating process. **Requires:** SME-30/48; MSF-04 only for the explicit dominated reference likelihood; continuous-time filtration/predictability. **Sources:** Rasmussen full 19 pp., Props.2.1,2.2,3.1; unread/failed source records are not evidence.

audited_existing_suppliers.current_item_clause_excerpt_verbatim:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. On a probability space
$(\Omega,\mathcal F,P)$, a **continuous-time filtration** is a family
$(\mathcal F_t)_{t\ge0}$ of sub-sigma-algebras of $\mathcal F$ such that
$\mathcal F_s\subseteq\mathcal F_t$ whenever $0\le s\le t$. A process
$X=(X_t)_{t\ge0}$ is **adapted** when $X_t$ is measurable from
$(\Omega,\mathcal F_t)$ to its state space at every $t$.

For any process of random elements $X=(X_t)_{t\ge0}$, its **natural
filtration** is

$$\mathcal F_t^X=\sigma\!\left(\{X_u^{-1}(C):0\le u\le t,\ C\text{ measurable in the state space of }X_u\}\right).$$

The generated sigma-algebra exists by
[[thm-generated-sigma-algebra-exists-and-is-minimal]]. Its generator families
are nested in $t$, so $(\mathcal F_t^X)_{t\ge0}$ is a filtration; every
$X_t$ is $\mathcal F_t^X$-measurable, and minimality makes this the smallest
filtration to which $X$ is adapted. No completion or right-continuous
augmentation is included.

A real process $M=(M_t)_{t\ge0}$ is an **all-pairs continuous-time
martingale** relative to $(\mathcal F_t)$ when:

1. $M$ is adapted;
2. $E|M_t|<\infty$ for every $t\ge0$; and
3. for every $0\le s\le t$,
   $$E[M_t\mid\mathcal F_s]=M_s\qquad\text{almost surely}.$$

The equality in clause 3 is equality of the almost-everywhere classes in
[[def-conditional-expectation-as-an-ae-class]]. At $s=t$ it is the
known-variable identity. The word “continuous-time” specifies the index set;
it does not assert path continuity. Likewise the definition imposes neither
right continuity nor completeness on the filtration. AC is declared exactly
because the library's conditional-expectation existence theorem uses it; the
filtration, adaptation, and natural-filtration constructions make no choices.

continuous-time-filtration interface, whose separate martingale clause uses

times are given, the progressive and predictable constructions below make no
additional choice: they use only generated sigma-algebras and product
rectangles.

   **progressively measurable** relative to $(\mathcal F_t)$ when for every
   $t\ge0$ the restricted map
   $[0,t]\times\Omega\to\mathbb R$, $(s,\omega)\mapsto X_s(\omega)$, is
   measurable for the product sigma-algebra
   $\mathcal B([0,t])\otimes\mathcal F_t$

pairs.title: BY arbitrary dependence and BH PRDS
findings_and_repairs: Pair contract reviewed; exact claims, prerequisites, source ranges and proof obligations are transcribed below.
pairs.proposal_text_verbatim: **Pages:** fdr-control-under-dependence / fdr-control-under-dependence-examples. **A:** Define $H_m=\sum_{j=1}^m1/j$. Under arbitrary dependence among valid p-values, the BY step-up rule $p_{(k)}\le kq/(mH_m)$ has FDR $\le(m_0/m)q$, by summing null contributions over rejection counts with weights $1/k$. Separately define PRDS on the true-null coordinates: for each true-null $i$ and every coordinatewise increasing measurable set $D\subseteq[0,1]^m$, $x\mapsto P(P\in D\mid P_i=x)$ has a nondecreasing version on the support. Under this exact condition, ordinary BH $p_{(k)}\le kq/m$ has FDR $\le(m_0/m)q$. Prove by the BY harmonic argument and the source PRDS monotonicity lemma, respectively. Pairwise positive correlation is not PRDS; two-sided Gaussian tests have no blanket guarantee. **B:** available dependence premise and threshold comparison. **Requires:** SME-52/54; MSF-08; exact PRDS definition. **Sources:** BY01 PRDS definition p.4, BY pp.5,18–19, PRDS pp.13–16; full paper.

pairs.title: Polyhedral selective inference
findings_and_repairs: Pair contract reviewed; exact claims, prerequisites, source ranges and proof obligations are transcribed below.
pairs.proposal_text_verbatim: **Pages:** polyhedral-selective-inference / polyhedral-selective-inference-examples. **A:** Let fixed $Y\sim N_n(\mu,\sigma^2I_n)$, known $\sigma>0$, nonzero fixed $\eta\in\mathbb R^n$, and selection event $S=\{AY\le b\}$ with $P_\mu(S)>0$. Set $T=\eta^TY$, $\theta=\eta^T\mu$, $Z=(I-\eta\eta^T/\|\eta\|^2)Y$; then $T\perp Z$, and conditional on $Z$, the polyhedron restricts $T$ to an interval $[L(Z),U(Z)]$, possibly with infinite endpoints. Conditional on $Z,S$, $T$ is $N(\theta,\sigma^2\|\eta\|^2)$ truncated to that interval. Its conditional CDF pivot $\{\Phi((T-\theta)/s)-\Phi((L-\theta)/s)\}/\{\Phi((U-\theta)/s)-\Phi((L-\theta)/s)\}$, $s=\sigma\|\eta\|$, is Uniform$(0,1)$ conditional on $Z,S$ wherever the truncation normalizer is positive. Invert this pivot for exact selective tests/confidence sets; no unknown-variance, nonlinear/nonpolyhedral selection or selected-family simultaneous guarantee. **B:** choose larger of two normal means. **Requires:** MSF-08/10; published Gaussian orthogonal projection/normal-law clauses (AC inherited). **Sources:** Lee et al. 2016 Lemma 4.1, Prop.4.2, Lemma 5.1, Thms.5.2/6.1/App.A, full article; Fithian–Sun–Taylor focused pp.1–10,15–16.

audited_existing_suppliers.current_item_clause_excerpt_verbatim: Assume AC and let $d\ge1$ be finite. For $m\in\mathbb R^d$ and a real symmetric positive semidefinite matrix $\Sigma$, a Borel probability law is denoted $N_d(m,\Sigma)$ when a vector X with that law satisfies $u\cdot X\sim N(u\cdot m,u^T\Sigma u)$ for every $u\in\mathbb R^d$. Such a law exists, has mean m and covariance Sigma, and can be realized as $m+\Sigma^{1/2}Z$ with independent standard-normal coordinates. Singular Sigma is allowed. Uniqueness will be proved in the following characteristic-function lemma.

audited_existing_suppliers.current_item_clause_excerpt_verbatim: Assume AC. Define $\gamma(E)=\int_E e^{-x^2/2}/\sqrt{2\pi}\,dx$ for Borel E in $\mathbb R$. By [[lem-normal-density-has-total-mass-one]] and [[thm-indefinite-integral-of-a-nonnegative-function-is-a-measure]], gamma is a probability measure; denote it $N(0,1)$. For $m\in\mathbb R$ and $\sigma\ge0$, define $N(m,\sigma^2)$ as the law of $x\mapsto m+\sigma x$ on $(\mathbb R,\mathcal B,\gamma)$. This affine map is continuous: for $\sigma$>0 choose $\delta$=$\varepsilon$/$\sigma$, and for $\sigma$=0 it is constant. Its inverse images of opens are open, so it is Borel measurable. [[lem-law-of-a-random-element-is-a-probability-measure]] makes its pushforward a probability. When $\sigma$=0, the preimage of E is all of R if m belongs to E and empty otherwise, so $N(m,0)=\delta_m$ in [[def-dirac-measure]].

pairs.proposal_text_verbatim: **Pages:** reproducibility-replication-and-transparent-reporting / reproducibility-replication-and-transparent-reporting-examples. **A:** Adopt the National Academies convention explicitly: computational reproducibility compares results using the same input data, code/computational methods and analysis conditions; replicability compares studies aimed at the same question using each study's new data; generalizability concerns other contexts/populations. Define transparent reporting as identifying data/code where lawful and ethical, computational environment, curation, methods and analysis decisions, exploratory/confirmatory status, and uncertainty. Record that usage varies across fields and this page adopts this convention. These are definitions/recommendations, not a theorem about correctness or future replication; exact reproduction can repeat an error. **B:** same raw data, alternate documented grouping and an independent study with new data. **Requires:** none beyond model/study terminology. **Sources:** NASEM Ch.3 Conclusion 3-1 pp.45–46, discussion pp.46–52, Box 3-2/Finding 3-1 pp.53–54; full chapter. pairs.title: Sequential likelihood-ratio tests
findings_and_repairs: Pair contract reviewed; exact claims, prerequisites, source ranges and proof obligations are transcribed below.
pairs.proposal_text_verbatim: **Pages:** sequential-likelihood-ratio-tests / sequential-likelihood-ratio-tests-examples. **A:** Separate three items: a procedure algorithm, two terminal-error bounds, and an iid termination theorem. For simple $H_0:P_0$ versus $H_1:P_1$ on filtration $(\mathcal F_t)$, assume mutually equivalent restrictions $P_0|_{\mathcal F_t}\sim P_1|_{\mathcal F_t}$ for each finite $t$, with consistent density process $L_t=dP_1|_{\mathcal F_t}/dP_0|_{\mathcal F_t}$. For $0<\alpha,\beta<1$, define $\tau=\inf\{t\ge1:L_t\ge1/\alpha\text{ or }L_t\le\beta\}$, decide $H_1$ at the upper boundary and $H_0$ at the lower; nontermination remains possible absent the separate theorem. Under $P_0$, $L_t$ is a nonnegative mean-one martingale; under $P_1$, $1/L_t$ is one. Ville gives $P_0(\tau<\infty,L_\tau\ge1/\alpha)\le\alpha$ and $P_1(\tau<\infty,L_\tau\le\beta)\le\beta$, without finite stopping. For iid observations with mutually equivalent one-observation laws and $Z=\log(dP_1/dP_0)(X)$, if $E_0|Z|,E_1|Z|<\infty$ and $E_0Z<0<E_1Z$, the iid strong law yields $\log L_t/t\to E_0Z<0$ under $P_0$ and $E_1Z>0$ under $P_1$, so $\tau<\infty$ a.s. under each law. Error control and termination are distinct; no expected-time optimality or exact Wald approximate-boundary claim. **B:** Bernoulli simple hypotheses with product likelihood ratio; compute error crossings and verify stopping under the drift conditions. **Requires:** MSF-04 likelihood-ratio RN derivative/change of measure; MSF-34 test-supermartingale/Ville; published bounded optional sampling and iid L1 strong law. **Sources:** Wolpert Duke notes pp. 1–5, 13–16 discuss SPRT and mark Wald cutoffs approximate; Howard 2020 supports the supermartingale boundary argument; existing finite-horizon ex-stopping-a-likelihood-ratio-martingale is only a cross-check. The two-boundary properties and iid termination proof are local.

pairs.title: Sub-Gaussian mixture confidence sequences
findings_and_repairs: Pair contract reviewed; exact claims, prerequisites, source ranges and proof obligations are transcribed below.
pairs.proposal_text_verbatim: **Pages:** subgaussian-mixture-confidence-sequences / subgaussian-mixture-confidence-sequences-examples. **A:** For adapted real $X_t$, fixed $\mu$, filtration $\mathcal F_t$, known $\sigma^2>0$, assume for every $\lambda\in\mathbb R$, $E[e^{\lambda(X_t-\mu)}\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}]\le e^{\lambda^2\sigma^2/2}$. Define $S_t=\sum_{i=1}^t(X_i-\mu)$, $\bar X_t=t^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^tX_i$, $V_t=t\sigma^2$, and choose $\rho>0,\alpha\in(0,1)$. Mixing the exponential supermartingales over $N(0,1/\rho)$ gives $M_t=\sqrt{\rho/(V_t+\rho)}e^{S_t^2/[2(V_t+\rho)]}$. By completing the square, $M_t\ge1/\alpha$ iff $|S_t|\ge u_\alpha(V_t)$, $u_\alpha(v)=\sqrt{(v+\rho)\log((v+\rho)/(\alpha^2\rho))}$. Thus define $C_t=[\bar X_t-u_\alpha(t\sigma^2)/t,\bar X_t+u_\alpha(t\sigma^2)/t]$, and Ville gives $P_\mu(\mu\in C_t\ \forall t\ge1)\ge1-\alpha$. The proxy must satisfy the conditional mgf bound; marginal sub-Gaussianity or a variance bound alone is insufficient. **B:** Gaussian increments versus invalid marginal-only sub-Gaussian claim. **Requires:** SME-58; MSF-34 mixture/CS; conditional Tonelli. **Sources:** Howard 2021 focused pp.1–9,27–28; Howard 2020 pp.9–18,45.

audited_existing_suppliers.current_item_clause_excerpt_verbatim:
Let $(\Omega,\mathcal F,P)$ be a probability space, $\mathcal G\subseteq\mathcal F$ a sub-sigma-algebra, and $X:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ integrable. A **conditional-expectation version of $X$ given $\mathcal G$** is a real, $\mathcal G$-measurable, integrable function $Y$ such that $\int_A Y\,dP=\int_A X\,dP$ for every $A\in\mathcal G$. No completeness of $\mathcal G$ is assumed.

Expectation means the integral of [[def-expectation-of-a-nonnegative-or-integrable-random-variable]]. Integrable representatives use [[def-l-one-of-a-measure]]; quotient notation is introduced after uniqueness.

audited_existing_suppliers.current_item_clause_excerpt_verbatim:
Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ and $(Y,\mathcal B,\nu)$ be sigma-finite measure
spaces, and let $f : X \times Y \to [0,\infty]$ be product-measurable. Then
$x \mapsto \int_Y f_x\,d\nu$ and $y \mapsto \int_X f^y\,d\mu$ are measurable,
and

$$\int_{X \times Y} f\,d(\mu \times \nu) = \int_X \left(\int_Y f_x\,d\nu\right)d\mu = \int_Y \left(\int_X f^y\,d\mu\right)d\nu.$$

pairs.title: Group-sequential alpha spending
findings_and_repairs: Specified the canonical zero-mean Gaussian vector/covariance (without incorrectly assigning independent increments to standardized statistics), alpha domain, t0=0, and infinite boundary for flat spending.
pairs.proposal_text_verbatim: **Pages:** group-sequential-alpha-spending / group-sequential-alpha-spending-examples. **A:** Specify maximum $K$, prescheduled information fractions $0<t_1<\cdots<t_K=1$, nondecreasing spending function $A:[0,1]\to[0,\alpha]$ for $\alpha\in(0,1)$ with $A(0)=0,A(1)=\alpha$, and the one-sided canonical Gaussian null vector $Z\sim N_K(0,\Sigma)$ with zero mean and $\Sigma_{jk}=\sqrt{t_j/t_k}$ for $j\le k$ (and symmetry for $j>k$). Set $t_0=0$ and define the boundary algorithm recursively by $\Pr_0(\max_{j\le k}Z_j\ge b_j)=A(t_k)$; when $A(t_k)=A(t_{k-1})$ set $b_k=+\infty$, and when spending increases choose the finite boundary under the stated joint law. This gives exact cumulative type-I spending at each planned look and total $\alpha$; two-sided designs use separately calibrated two-sided crossing events. Exactness is conditional on this joint law and prespecified looks; data-dependent timing/estimated variance requires a new calibration argument. **B:** named spending functions under canonical law. **Requires:** MSF-08; published `def-multivariate-normal-law`, `def-standard-normal-and-normal-laws`, and `lem-normal-density-has-total-mass-one` (AC for the Gaussian-law supplier). **Sources:** DeMets–Lan 1994 pp.2–3,6–7,9; Grayling–Wason–Mander 2018 pp.2–4; Minas Ch.5 5.3–5.3.1 printed pp.72–74.

audited_existing_suppliers.current_item_clause_excerpt_verbatim: Assume AC and let $d\ge1$ be finite. For $m\in\mathbb R^d$ and a real symmetric positive semidefinite matrix $\Sigma$, a Borel probability law is denoted $N_d(m,\Sigma)$ when a vector X with that law satisfies $u\cdot X\sim N(u\cdot m,u^T\Sigma u)$ for every $u\in\mathbb R^d$. Such a law exists, has mean m and covariance Sigma, and can be realized as $m+\Sigma^{1/2}Z$ with independent standard-normal coordinates. Singular Sigma is allowed. Uniqueness will be proved in the following characteristic-function lemma.

audited_existing_suppliers.reusable_clause_exact: Scalar normal laws and density normalization; the normal-law definition is homed here rather than on the CLT page. Positive variance is required for exact Student/F denominators.
audited_existing_suppliers.current_item_clause_excerpt_verbatim: Assume AC. Define $\gamma(E)=\int_E e^{-x^2/2}/\sqrt{2\pi}\,dx$ for Borel E in $\mathbb R$. By [[lem-normal-density-has-total-mass-one]] and [[thm-indefinite-integral-of-a-nonnegative-function-is-a-measure]], gamma is a probability measure; denote it $N(0,1)$. For $m\in\mathbb R$ and $\sigma\ge0$, define $N(m,\sigma^2)$ as the law of $x\mapsto m+\sigma x$ on $(\mathbb R,\mathcal B,\gamma)$. This affine map is continuous: for $\sigma$>0 choose $\delta$=$\varepsilon$/$\sigma$, and for $\sigma$=0 it is constant. Its inverse images of opens are open, so it is Borel measurable. [[lem-law-of-a-random-element-is-a-probability-measure]] makes its pushforward a probability. When $\sigma$=0, the preimage of E is all of R if m belongs to E and empty otherwise, so $N(m,0)=\delta_m$ in [[def-dirac-measure]].

pairs.title: Two-stage conditional-error adaptation
findings_and_repairs: Pair contract reviewed; exact claims, prerequisites, source ranges and proof obligations are transcribed below.
pairs.proposal_text_verbatim: **Pages:** two-stage-conditional-error-adaptation / two-stage-conditional-error-adaptation-examples. **A:** For a fixed null law $P_0$ and interim sigma-algebra $\mathcal F_1$, define the original conditional error $A= P_0(\text{original rejection}\mid\mathcal F_1)$, assuming $E_0A\le\alpha$. If an adapted design has conditional probability of any eventual rejection at most $A$ a.s., then $P_0(\text{adapted rejection})\le\alpha$ by the tower property. A sufficient implementation is a stage-2 p-value satisfying $P_0(p_2\le u\mid\mathcal F_1)\le u$ a.s. for every $u\in[0,1]$, with rejection rule $p_2\le A$. Fresh stage-2 data independent under the conditional null is one sufficient route, but the selected-sample-size conditional law must be stated. This covers single-hypothesis sample-size/continuation adaptation; treatment-allocation learning, endpoint selection and multiarm adaptive selection are excluded. **B:** calibrated sample-size adaptation versus changed combination weights without conditional recalibration. **Requires:** MSF-08; published conditional-expectation tower (AC). **Sources:** Sugiura–Uesaka 2008 pp.6–9; Minas Ch.5 5.4.1–5.4.2 printed pp.74–79, complete chapter.

audited_existing_suppliers.current_item_clause_excerpt_verbatim:
Let $(\Omega,\mathcal F,P)$ be a probability space, $\mathcal G\subseteq\mathcal F$ a sub-sigma-algebra, and $X:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ integrable. A **conditional-expectation version of $X$ given $\mathcal G$** is a real, $\mathcal G$-measurable, integrable function $Y$ such that $\int_A Y\,dP=\int_A X\,dP$ for every $A\in\mathcal G$. No completeness of $\mathcal G$ is assumed.

Expectation means the integral of [[def-expectation-of-a-nonnegative-or-integrable-random-variable]]. Integrable representatives use [[def-l-one-of-a-measure]]; quotient notation is introduced after uniqueness.

audited_existing_suppliers.current_item_clause_excerpt_verbatim: Assume AC for existence. If $\mathcal H\subseteq\mathcal G\subseteq\mathcal F$ and $X\in L^1(P)$, then $E[E[X\mid\mathcal G]\mid\mathcal H]=E[X\mid\mathcal H]$ and $E[E[X\mid\mathcal H]\mid\mathcal G]=E[X\mid\mathcal H]$ almost surely. Also, if a version of $E[X\mid\mathcal G]$ is $\mathcal H$-measurable, it is a version of $E[X\mid\mathcal H]$.
